bbc.description: The ship was reportedly struck by an "unknown projectile" near Oman but no casualties were reported.

bbc.description: But the budget faces an uphill battle as the president spars with some members of his own party over the issue.

bbc.description: Prosecutors say Vusimusi "Cat" Matlala could provide evidence against "high-ranking officials".

bbc.title: Oil price falls back to pre-Iran war levels
bbc.description: Signs that traffic through the key Strait of Hormuz shipping route is gradually resuming has helped to push the oil price down.

bbc.title: IBM hails new 'block of flats' design breakthrough for ultra tiny chips
bbc.description: IBM says it has created the world's first known chip tech below 1 nanometre - but it will be some time before it's ready for production.

bbc.title: Ryanair says it will reluctantly not charge parents to sit next to children
bbc.description: The airline had typically charged adults a fee of £8 each way to sit with their young children.

bbc.description: Protesters demand justice for the dozens killed during the 2024 demonstrations and last year's anniversary protests.

bbc.description: The rare school shooting that left three students killed and 20 others injured has shocked the country.

bbc.description: The firm alleged that Alibaba used fraudulent accounts to access data from its Claude AI model.

bbc.title: Independent MPs launch new Australian centrist party
bbc.description: Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender say Community Strong Australia will offer citizens 'reason over rage'.

bbc.title: Clean sweep for Mamdani-backed candidates in New York's Democratic primary
bbc.description: Brad Lander unseats Dan Goldman in a race that laid bare the city's divisions over the Israel-Gaza war.

bbc.title: Air conditioning creates political divide after France records hottest day
bbc.description: France is being forced to re-think its longstanding reservations about air-conditioning as temperatures soar.

bbc.title: Biggest city in Crimea without power after Ukraine strikes
bbc.description: Sevastopol's Moscow-installed governor warns there will be no electricity in some areas until the evening.

bbc.description: Rafael Grossi says the IAEA is "working on modalities" but an Iranian  minister says such access would only be part of a final deal with the US.

rfi.title: Fear of mines alone could disrupt Strait of Hormuz shipping, warns French admiral
rfi.description: The Strait of Hormuz has reopened under a fragile United States-Iran deal, but it remains under close watch after maritime authorities warned of suspected and confirmed mines in the area. Former French Navy Admiral Éric Lavault – who headed France's mine warfare and seabed operations, and commanded the navy's bomb-disposal divers – told RFI that even without proof the strait has been mined, it must be checked before commercial shipping can return to normal.

rfi.title: Paris court gives oil giant TotalEnergies deadline to tighten climate policies
rfi.description: A court in Paris ruled on Thursday that energy giant TotalEnergies must account for its consumers’ greenhouse gas emissions, giving the French company six months to adjust a legally mandated risk assessment.

rfi.title: France told to do more to protect children from human trafficking
rfi.description: France must step up efforts to prevent human trafficking and improve support for victims, particularly children and young people, the Council of Europe has said, warning that weaknesses in the country's child protection system continue to leave minors exposed to exploitation.

rfi.title: Relief in sight as temperatures set to fall in France after record heatwave
rfi.description: Temperatures are expected to fall in France from Thursday evening after another day of extreme heat that put 72 of mainland France's 96 departments on red alert, affecting more than 50 million people.

rfi.title: South African anti-migrant groups defend planned ‘Liberation March’
rfi.description: A coalition of South African organisations campaigning against undocumented migrants has defended its plans for nationwide demonstrations on 30 June, insisting the marches will be peaceful despite rising tensions and recent deadly unrest.

rfi.title: Kenya mounts huge security operation on Gen Z protest anniversary
rfi.description: Kenyan police put on a massive show of force Thursday in a bid to prevent protests marking two years since a landmark Gen Z uprising.

rfi.title: Macron to host Meloni in Antibes as France and Italy seek closer ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the French seaside resort of Antibes, as the two leaders try to revive a relationship that has been marked by political differences.

rfi.title: Zelensky to miss Poland summit as Second World War row escalates
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will not attend a major conference on rebuilding Ukraine being held in Poland this week, as a dispute between the two countries over Second World War remembrance threatens to overshadow talks.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Thapelo Maseko scored mid way through the second half against South Korea to take South Africa into the knockout stages at a World Cup for the first time.

rfi.title: Digital euro wins key EU backing as lawmakers approve draft rules
rfi.description: The European Union has moved a step closer to creating a digital euro, after members of the European Parliament passed a crucial vote on the virtual currency.

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

rfi.title: France announces first Ebola case in doctor returned from DR Congo
rfi.description: French health authorities on Wednesday announced the first confirmed case of Ebola identified on national territory – a doctor who had returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

rfi.title: Switzerland outwit Canada to claim Group B at 2026 World Cup
rfi.description: Switzerland claimed top spot in Group B at the World Cup on Wednesday following a 2-1 win over Canada in Vancouver.

rfi.title: Seven European countries urge ‘immediate halt’ to Sudan violence
rfi.description: Seven European countries have called on Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to immediately stop their assault on El-Obeid, a city in Sudan's North Kordofan state, warning of credible signs that a major offensive could be imminent as civilians face worsening shortages of food, water and fuel.

rfi.title: Portugal delays handover of French mother accused of abandoning children
rfi.description: Portuguese authorities have refused to immediately extradite to France a 41-year-old woman suspected of abandoning her two young children, who were found last month crying at the side of a road south of Lisbon.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch was inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday in a sombre ceremony, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the country’s most symbolic events.

rfi.title: French government begins disciplinary action over child abuse case failings
rfi.description: The French government has announced disciplinary action against a magistrate and two gendarmerie officers over the handling of a suspect in child abuse case, which has lead to public outcry. This comes on the heels of a report which pointed to serious failings of the justice system, particularly with regards to minors.

euronews.title: US Supreme Court clears way for mass deportations of Haitians and Syrians
euronews.description: The 6-3 ruling hands Donald Trump a sweeping victory on immigration, stripping legal protections from hundreds of thousands of people the State Department warns would be returning to dangerous countries.

euronews.title: EU's door 'is open to UK', fomer Brexit negotiator Barnier tells Euronews
euronews.description: Ten years following the landmark vote, the EU's former Brexit negotiator said the bloc's door is open to the UK, but that London "cannot cherry-pick" EU policies.

euronews.title: Binance to halt crypto services across EU countries after failing to secure MiCA approval
euronews.description: The world's largest crypto exchange is pulling out of multiple EU markets after withdrawing its Greek licence application before a June 30 deadline.

euronews.description: The British military said a cargo ship on the new Omani UN-backed route sustained bridge damage from a projectile, hours after the IRGC warned that vessels without Iranian permission were transiting "illegally".

euronews.title: French heatwave: three-year-old found dead in car
euronews.description: The boy climbed into the unlocked car while out of his parents' sight; his mother was hospitalised in shock. Two other children died in Carpentras on Monday.

euronews.description: The European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) has presented a proposal for European legislation to protect workers' health during heatwaves.

euronews.description: Rutte pushed back gently against Trump's latest NATO complaints, saying, “I know there have been isolated cases about which you are really disappointed, but generally speaking, your European allies have been there with you."

euronews.title: France takes nuclear reactors offline amid record heatwave
euronews.description: EDF cites environmental rules protecting river ecosystems as rising water temperatures force output cuts at sites on the Seine and Rhone.

euronews.title: 'I'm in great shape,' boxing legend Floyd Mayweather tells Euronews ahead of Athens fight
euronews.description: Floyd "Money" Mayweather was set to face Greek fighter Mike Zambidis in Athens on Saturday 27 June but the bout was postponed for September.

euronews.title: La Guaira, Venezuela’s port city, shows extensive earthquake damage after the quake
euronews.description: New images from La Guaira on 25 June revealed widespread destruction after twin earthquakes struck Venezuela's Caribbean coast, damaging buildings, roads and key public infrastructure.

euronews.title: Brussels tightens rules on US cloud providers as it pushes for tech sovereignty
euronews.description: The European Commission has decided that Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services should face strict rules to improve cloud competition. The move risks angering Washington as Brussels pushes the European tech sovereignty agenda.

euronews.title: James Bond search enters final stage with planned August screen tests
euronews.description: Production on Bond 26 is set to begin next year. The expectation is that the official announcement for the next 007 actor will happen by the end of 2026.

euronews.description: Youssoupha acknowledged cyberbullying and harassment were part of the challenges facing young Africans today, but he urged the youth to focus on the positives.

euronews.title: Moment French navy boards suspected Russian 'ghost fleet' tanker
euronews.description: The French navy boarded a tanker suspected of belonging to Russia's so-called "ghost fleet" in the Mediterranean, the fifth such operation since September 2025, as Paris steps up efforts to enforce sanctions linked to the war in Ukraine.

guardian.title: Papua New Guinea at risk of food shortages as El Niño brings frost and drought
guardian.description:
Oxfam predicts PNG will be worst-hit country in Pacific from the weather pattern, with up to 3 million people affected nationwide

Families across Papua New Guinea’s Highlands are facing depleted harvests and the threat of hunger after the El Niño weather pattern brought frost and prolonged dry conditions that have destroyed food gardens providing sustenance and income for thousands of households.

British disinfectant brand withdraws advert about a man’s efforts to find a ‘clean and untouched’ woman

The British hygiene brand Dettol has apologised after an advertisement released in China, which it said was intended to criticise “toxic men”, was widely condemned on social media as offensive to women.

The five-minute advert for a multipurpose disinfectant, released across many online platforms at the end of May, features a man comparing his girlfriend with his former partner.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : le préfet de Paris alerte sur des hôpitaux « saturés » ; la consommation d’alcool interdite sur la voie publique dans la capitale dès demain midi
lemonde.description: Le préfet de police a souligné que « le nombre d’hospitalisations ne cesse d’augmenter ». Par ailleurs, les chiffres de la surmortalité ne seront connus officiellement que dans quelques mois, mais des morts sont déjà imputées à la chaleur par certaines préfectures ou les forces de l’ordre.

lemonde.title: Les dessous de « Legend », le média en ligne de Guillaume Pley qui pourrait peser dans la campagne présidentielle
lemonde.description: Le fondateur de « Legend », Guillaume Pley, se targue de proposer des vidéos d’interviews bienveillantes, neutres et qui parlent à tout le monde. Notre analyse d’une année entière d’émissions et les témoignages exclusifs recueillis auprès d’anciens salariés racontent une réalité bien différente.

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : au moins 188 morts et plus de 1 500 blessés, selon un nouveau bilan provisoire
lemonde.description: Deux tremblements de terre, dont l’un devenu le plus puissant en plus d’un siècle dans le pays, ont frappé l’ouest de Caracas, dans la soirée de mercredi. Les spécialistes redoutent un bilan « lourd » et des dégâts « importants ».

lemonde.title: La Cour suprême américaine autorise un éventuel renvoi des demandeurs d’asile à la frontière avec le Mexique
lemonde.description: L’administration de Donald Trump peut désormais renouer avec une politique, lancée en 2016 et suspendue sous Joe Biden, consistant à empêcher les migrants de franchir la frontière avec le Mexique pour déposer leur demande d’asile aux Etats-Unis.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Equateur-Allemagne et Curaçao-Côte d’Ivoire : la Tri égalise contre la Mannschaft, les Eléphants ont ouvert la marque avec Nicolas Pépé
lemonde.description: Pour la troisième et dernière journée dans le groupe E, jeudi 25 juin, l’Equateur tentera de battre l’Allemagne pour se qualifier pour les 16ᵉˢ de finale. L’enjeu est le même pour Curaçao contre la Côte d’Ivoire.

lemonde.title: Emoi à France Culture après la diffusion d’un audio « fallacieux » de « Leon le média » visant Jean-Luc Mélenchon
lemonde.description: La station publique a diffusé, mercredi 25 juin, lors d’une interview de Marine Le Pen dans la matinale de Guillaume Erner, le son d’un pure-player militant mettant en parallèle des déclarations antisémites de Jean-Marie Le Pen et des propos détournés du candidat des insoumis à la présidentielle.

lemonde.title: Détroit d’Ormuz : le plan d’évacuation suspendu à la suite d’une attaque dans le golfe d’Oman
lemonde.description: Plus tôt dans la journée, l’agence de sécurité maritime britannique UKMTO rapportait qu’« un cargo a[vait] été touché à tribord par un projectile non identifié, ce qui a endommagé la passerelle », sans faire de blessé.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : fin d’alerte aérienne à Kiev après plusieurs explosions ; des débris tombés dans un quartier de la capitale
lemonde.description: Des journalistes de l’Agence France-Presse (AFP) avaient fait état d’explosions dans la capitale ukrainienne. Une chute d’épave a eu lieu « dans le raïon Darnytsky, en plein air. Il est probable qu’il y aura d’autres lieux d’impact », a rapporté le chef de l’administration militaire de la capitale.

lemonde.title: Liban : Emmanuel Macron et Giorgia Meloni veulent une coalition multinationale à la fin du mandat de la Finul
lemonde.description: L’Italie et la France « peuvent absolument faire la différence. (…) Il est nécessaire de garantir une présence internationale qui évite un vide sécuritaire extrêmement dangereux », a notamment déclaré la première ministre italienne.

lemonde.title: Trois juges ripostent contre les sanctions à leur encontre, espérant voir le décret américain anti-CPI suspendu
lemonde.description: Depuis le décret signé par Donald Trump le 6 février 2025, au lendemain de la visite du premier ministre israélien à la Maison Blanche, 11 magistrats de la Cour pénale internationale ont été sanctionnés. Trois d’entre eux viennent de saisir la justice fédérale américaine.

lemonde.title: Roundup : la Cour suprême des Etats-Unis donne raison à Bayer face aux milliers de plaintes pour risque de cancer
lemonde.description: Le géant allemand s’est félicité de la décision en faveur de son herbicide, à base de glyphosate, accusé d’être cancérigène et à l’origine de procès coûtant plus de 10 milliards de dollars au groupe.

lemonde.title: Liste de « génocidaires à boycotter » : le professeur de l’université Lyon-II Julien Théry condamné par la section disciplinaire
lemonde.description: Le jugement, publié mercredi 24 juin, pointe plusieurs publications à caractère discriminatoire de l’historien sur les réseaux sociaux, conduisant à une sanction lourde : dix-huit mois d’interdiction d’enseigner avec privation de traitement.

lemonde.title: Métro : de nouveaux retards pour les lignes 15 et 18 du Grand Paris Express
lemonde.description: L’ouverture du premier morceau de la ligne entre Massy et Saclay, prévue le 1er octobre, est décalée d’au moins deux mois. Le délai est de six mois pour la ligne 15 sud, dont la mise en service était prévue au printemps 2027.

lemonde.title: Sous pression, le gouvernement renonce à renforcer les pouvoirs des préfets
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement a décidé, jeudi 25 juin, de retirer de l’ordre du jour du Sénat son projet de loi visant à « renforcer l’Etat local ». Le texte suscitait de nombreuses réserves parmi les élus locaux et les sénateurs. L’exécutif dit prioriser son texte sur « la relance et la décentralisation du logement ».

lemonde.title: Procès climatique contre TotalEnergies : la justice ordonne au groupe pétrolier de prendre en compte les émissions de CO₂ de ses clients
lemonde.description: Depuis 2020, une coalition d’associations et la Ville de Paris demandent à la justice de contraindre la multinationale à réduire ses émissions de gaz à effet de serre. Le tribunal vient d’exiger que le géant pétrogazier intègre dans son plan de vigilance les émissions de ses clients. Une avancée significative.

lemonde.title: IA : le test d’un modèle chinois à la direction générale du Trésor interrompu à cause de « réponses orientées » ou « biaisées »
lemonde.description: Baptisé « HéphAIstos » en référence au dieu grec, l’outil comprend un agent conversationnel pour assister les hauts fonctionnaires dans leurs tâches quotidiennes, y compris pour le traitement de données confidentielles ou sensibles. Un nouveau modèle de la start-up française Mistral AI a été installé mercredi.

lemonde.title: Que célèbrent les musulmans lors de l’Achoura ?
lemonde.description: Les musulmans observent, vendredi, cette tradition qui remonte aux tout premiers temps de l’islam et s’inspire de la fête juive de Yom Kippour.

lemonde.title: « François d’Assise, la sainteté est un sport de combat », sur France Culture : une « Grande Traversée » pour dévoiler l’homme derrière le saint
lemonde.description: L’enquête en cinq volets de Céline Laurens rappelle que, avant de devenir l’une des figures majeures du christianisme, il fut un jeune homme en rupture avec son milieu et son époque.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Mbappé - Haaland, enfin le choc de titans tant attendu ?
france24fr.description: La première place du groupe I va se jouer vendredi entre la France et la Norvège. Ce choc entre ces deux pays invaincus depuis le début du Mondial va aussi être l'occasion de voir s'affronter deux des plus grands attaquants du monde : Kylian Mbappé et Erling Haaland. Ils se rencontrent pour la première fois en sélection nationale.

france24fr.title: "L'audiovisuel public est attaqué de toute part"
france24fr.description: Nathalie Sonnac, ancienne membre du Conseil supérieur de l'audiovisuel (CSA), professeure à l’université Paris Panthéon-Assas, spécialiste de l'économie des médias et du numérique est l'auteur de l'ouvrage : "Qui veut la peau de l'audiovisuel public ?" paru le 21 mai aux éditions de l'Observatoire. Son constat : l'audiovisuel public est mis sous pression notamment par le rassemblement national, alors qu'il est un luxe dont les démocraties ne peuvent se passer.

france24fr.title: Trump : la fin du leadership américain ?
france24fr.description: D. Trump rejette l’idée d’un déclin américain et a proclamé « America is back » lors du lancement des célébrations du 250ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance des États-Unis. Il a mis en avant plusieurs sujets, dont l’énergie, l’immigration, la Coupe du monde, mais aussi l’Iran et le détroit d’Ormuz, alors que les négociations avec Téhéran se poursuivent après la signature d’un accord de paix entre les deux pays. Pour l’Iran, ce protocole est d'ailleurs une "déclaration de défaite des États-Unis".

france24fr.title: Curaçao - Côte d'Ivoire en direct : les Éléphants ne perdent pas de temps, suivez le groupe E
france24fr.description: La Côte d'Ivoire doit sécuriser sa qualification pour les 16es de finale en affrontant Curaçao lors de la troisième journée du groupe E. Dans le même temps, l'Allemagne fait face à l'Équateur qui espère s'en sortir à la photo-finish. Suivez les deux matches en direct grâce au live commenté de nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les éléphants vers une qualification historique
france24fr.description:
Face à Curaçao, les Éléphants ont l'occasion de décrocher leur qualification et de mettre fin à une éventuelle malédiction.
 
Depuis Boston, notre envoyé spécial Cédric Ferreira vous fait vivre cette rencontre décisive.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Séismes au Venezuela en direct : le bilan s'alourdit à 188 morts, Delcy Rodriguez se rend sur place
Au Zimbabwe, le mandat présidentiel passe de 5 à 7 ans
france24fr.description: Au Zimbabwe, le Sénat a approuvé un projet de réforme constitutionnelle prévoyant notamment le passage du mandat présidentiel de 5 à 7 ans. Cette modification permettrait au président Emmerson Mnangagwa de rester au pouvoir jusqu'en 2030, sans organiser de nouvelle élection présidentielle.

france24fr.title: Dans les prisons françaises, la canicule aggrave une "catastrophe pénitentiaire"
france24fr.description: Dans des prisons surpeuplées, vétustes et mal adaptées aux fortes chaleurs, détenus comme surveillants pénitentiaires subissent de plein fouet l'épisode caniculaire qui frappe la France. Malgré les mesures d'urgence déployées par les autorités, cet épisode exceptionnel met en lumière une crise carcérale dénoncée depuis des années.

france24fr.title: Politique : Affaire Lyhanna, Marc Bloch au Panthéon et autonomie de la Corse
france24fr.description: Politique revient sur le prérapport dans la mort de Lyhanna et la plainte déposée précédemment contre Jérôme Barella. Ce rapport fait état de dysfonctionnements et de responsabilités individuelles. Il sera aussi question de la cérémonie d’entrée au Panthéon de Marc Bloch, présidée par Emmanuel Macron et de l’autonomie de la Corse. Pour débattre de ces sujets, Marc Perelman reçoit Catherine Tricot de la revue Regards, Stéphane Vernay de Ouest France et Roland Cayrol, politologue.

france24fr.title: Non, Ibrahim Traoré n’a pas critiqué la Coupe du monde 2026
france24fr.description: Une vidéo virale attribue à Ibrahim Traoré, président du Burkina Faso, un discours virulent sur la Coupe du monde 2026 et les États-Unis. Mais les images ont été détournées, l’audio modifié et les propos inventés. L’intox a été largement relayée sur les réseaux sociaux.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : découvrez le parcours incroyable d'Aymen Hussein
france24fr.description: Il est devenu le visage du football irakien. Pourtant, son histoire dépasse largement le sport.  Aymen Hussein a grandi dans un Irak marqué par la guerreet le terrorisme. À 12 ans, il perd son père, tué par Al-Qaïda. Six ans plus tard, son frère est capturé par l’organisation État islamique. Aymen pense à arrêter le football. Mais sa mère lui demande de continuer. Pendant des années, le football devient son refuge. Aymen Hussein finit par qualifier l'Irak pour sa première Coupe du monde depuis 1

france24fr.title: Que pensent les Égyptiens de Donald Trump ? Réponse avec Robert Solé
france24fr.description: Toutes les semaines, Judith Grimaldi reçoit un invité dans son émission "Avec Judith". Dans l'épisode de cette semaine, elle reçoit Robert Solé, journaliste et écrivain français d'origine égyptienne. Coptes, Frères musulmans, inégalités, fascination occidentale pour l'Égypte antique... il nous livre son analyse de la politique égyptienne et son évolution au cours des dernières années. Pour lui, "les Égyptiens ne savent plus ce que veut Donald Trump".

france24fr.title: TotalEnergies sommé d'inclure les émissions de ses clients dans sa stratégie climatique
france24fr.description: La justice a donné six mois à TotalEnergies pour intégrer dans son plan de vigilance les émissions de gaz à effet de serre générées par l’utilisation de ses produits par ses clients. Cette décision renforce les obligations climatiques des grandes entreprises et pourrait faire jurisprudence en matière de responsabilité environnementale. Les précisions de Marie Schuster.

france24fr.title: Le projet pétrolier controversé de TotalEnergies en Ouganda reste dans le viseur des ONG
france24fr.description: Parmi les projets visés par les ONG figure Tilenga-EACOP, un vaste projet pétrolier mené par TotalEnergies en Ouganda et en Tanzanie, critiqué pour ses impacts potentiels sur le climat, la biodiversité et les ressources en eau. Si le groupe met en avant ses retombées économiques et son engagement vers la neutralité carbone, ses opposants le qualifient de "bombe climatique", estimant qu'il pourrait générer 379 millions de tonnes de CO₂ sur vingt ans.

france24fr.title: L'Union européenne valide à contrecœur son accord commercial avec les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Les 27 États membres de l'Union européenne ont approuvé l'accord commercial conclu avec les États-Unis, mettant fin à plusieurs mois d'incertitude et de menaces de surtaxes brandies par Donald Trump. Malgré les critiques sur un texte jugé déséquilibré, les Européens ont privilégié le compromis afin de sécuriser des échanges transatlantiques représentant 1 700 milliards d'euros par an, avec une clause de réexamen prévue à la fin du mandat du président américain.

france24fr.title: France : la canicule, une "catastrophe nationale"
france24fr.description: Face à une canicule d'une intensité exceptionnelle, les hôpitaux français ont déclenché leur plan blanc, tandis que les services d'urgence, les pompiers et les centres d'appels du Samu font face à un afflux massif de demandes, jusqu'à quatre fois supérieur à la normale. Devant la saturation des secours et la multiplication des victimes, le Premier ministre a qualifié la situation de « catastrophe nationale ».

france24fr.title: La Cour suprême américaine ouvre la voie à l’expulsion de 350 000 Haïtiens
france24fr.description: La Cour suprême américaine a autorisé, jeudi, l'administration Trump à révoquer sans contrôle un statut protégeant 350 000 Haïtiens et 6 000 Syriens. Le président américain avait tenu des propos insultants envers les bénéficiaires de cette mesure, originaires, selon lui, de "pays de merde".

france24fr.title: Pourquoi les séismes qui ont frappé le Venezuela sont aussi inhabituels et dévastateurs
france24fr.description: La principale hypothèse retenue après le choc sismique qui a frappé le Venezuela, dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi, est la survenue d’un phénomène relativement rare : la succession très rapide et proche de deux secousses majeures “jumelles”.

spiegel.description: Mark Rutte gibt im Weißen Haus alles, um die Wogen zwischen Europa und den USA zu glätten. Trump zeigt sich unbeeindruckt – und erhöht den Druck vor dem kommenden Nato-Gipfel.

spiegel.title: Boris Pistorius: Ende des Marine-Großprojekts erhöht Druck auf Minister
spiegel.description: Das Ende des größten Rüstungsvorhabens der Marine zeigt die massiven Probleme bei der Beschaffung. Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius muss die Aufrüstung der Bundeswehr endlich zur Chefsache machen.

spiegel.title: Bund und Länder: Einigung auf Entlastung für Kommunen erzielt
spiegel.description: »Wer bestellt, bezahlt«: Diesem Grundsatz entsprechend forderten die Länder vom Bund eine neue Regelung, um die Kommunen bei bestimmten Gesetzen finanziell zu entlasten. Und hatten Erfolg.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: »Der Zug hat keine Bremse« wird zur inoffiziellen WM-Hymne

spiegel.title: »Medusa Protocol«: Was machen Auftragsmörder, wenn sie nicht mehr töten wollen?
spiegel.description: In einer New Yorker Kirche treffen sich die »Assassins Anonymous«, um über ihre Sünden zu sprechen und Buße zu tun. Bis plötzlich eine ihrer Kolleginnen in der brasilianischen Knasthölle landet.

spiegel.title: Vinted: Werden hier Kinder verkauft? Die absurde Debatte über dubiose Anzeigen
spiegel.description: Im Netz machen schwere Vorwürfe gegen die beliebte Second-Hand-Plattform Vinted die Runde. User, die sie verbreiten, sammeln Millionen Abrufe. Auch die Polizei beschäftigt sich damit. Die Hintergründe.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump und die 250-Jahres-Feier: »Er dringt nicht mehr durch«
spiegel.description: Trump tanzt, am Himmel fliegen Kampfjets – doch nur wenige schauen zu: Der Start der 250-Jahres-Feier in Washington lief nicht gut für den US-Präsidenten. Beobachtungen von SPIEGEL-Korrespondentin Britta Kollenbroich.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Wie eine Angriffsdrohung gegen Belarus Lukaschenko in Bedrängnis bringt
spiegel.description: Die Ukraine will Belarus zwingen, Signalverstärker abzubauen, mit deren Hilfe Russland seine Drohnenangriffe steuert. Diktator Lukaschenko scheint einzulenken, aber das könnte ihm Ärger mit Putin bescheren.

spiegel.title: Kibiwott Kandie: Lange Sperre nach verweigerter Dopingprobe und Fälschungen

spiegel.title: Tennis: Chris Evert macht erneute Krebserkrankung öffentlich

spiegel.title: AfD: Neues Gutachten bringt Bewegung in Verbotsdebatte

spiegel.title: Bundesgerichtshof verwirft Revisionen im Fall Mouhamed Dramé
spiegel.description: Der Prozess gegen fünf Polizisten wegen tödlicher Schüsse auf Mouhamed Dramé endete mit Freisprüchen. Nun sind Staatsanwaltschaft und Nebenklage mit ihren Revisionen gescheitert.

spiegel.title: KNDS: So viel bezahlt die Bundesregierung für den Einstieg beim Panzerhersteller
spiegel.description: Die Haushälter des Bundestags stimmen am Freitag über den Einstieg des Staates beim Panzerhersteller KNDS ab. Die Milliardensumme, die dafür fällig wird, dürfte nach SPIEGEL-Informationen für Diskussionen sorgen.

spiegel.title: Nato-Gipfel in der Türkei: Türkische Journalisten ausgeschlossen
spiegel.description: Kritische Presse unerwünscht? Vor dem Nato-Gipfel in Ankara sind viele türkische Reporter ohne Akkreditierung geblieben. Die Nato hat sich eigenen Angaben zufolge auf die Einschätzung des Gastgeberlandes verlassen.

spiegel.title: Tesla: Fertigungsziel steigt – weitere 1000 Jobs in Grünheide geplant
spiegel.description: Erst im April hatte der US-Elektroautobauer Tesla angekündigt, 1000 neue Mitarbeiter in seinem Werk in Grünheide beschäftigen zu wollen. Doch der Konzern will noch weiter expandieren.

observador.description: Francisco Calhas acredita que o prazo de 60 dias para um acordo nuclear é irrealista. Segundo o docente, os EUA só querem ganhar tempo e manter o estreito aberto até às eleições de novembro.

observador.title: Sismos são prova de fogo para Delcy Rodríguez

new-sci.title: Fluctuating oestrogen levels may alter how drugs enter women's brains
new-sci.description: Oestrogen levels fluctuate throughout a woman's menstrual cycle, which may impact how efficiently a drug that targets the brain can reach its destination

new-sci.title: Hidden black hole could explain mystery at the heart of our galaxy
new-sci.description: The area surrounding our galaxy’s central supermassive black hole contains three strangely different populations of stars – but one hidden black hole could explain all of them

new-sci.title: You should turn off fans when it's too hot – but how hot is too hot?
new-sci.description: Fans can make you hotter rather than cooler, but the temperature at which you should turn them off depends on several factors, including your age and the humidity level

phys-org.title: Dog's skull shape and body weight linked to spinal fluid disorder risk
phys-org.description: A new Cornell University study helps deepen the understanding of skull shapes in dogs of different sizes and draws a link between cranial and facial shapes, body weight, and the risk of syringomyelia, a spinal condition common in some dog breeds.

phys-org.title: Scientists measure hidden quantum forces that could power a new generation of pharmaceutical drugs
phys-org.description: It's one thing to design a pharmaceutical drug. It's another to know if and why it actually works; not on paper or in a computer model, but inside the chaotic world of living systems, where proteins twist into shape, atoms constantly pull and push each other apart, and molecular interactions are the difference between health and disease.

phys-org.title: Novel rice paddy approach aims to prevent toxic metals from tainting rice
phys-org.description: In a perspective published in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Colorado State University researchers describe a management approach to prevent the uptake of arsenic, cadmium and mercury in rice grains to protect human health. They propose strategies that would change soil chemistry in a way that immobilizes toxic metals and prevents plant uptake.

phys-org.title: Why AI rules in science matter now: Nature backs wider debate beyond mathematics
phys-org.description: In an editorial, Nature endorses the "Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics," which was published earlier this month by researchers from 15 different universities, including Rodrigo Ochigame (CADS) and David Holmes (FWN).

phys-org.title: Fossil fish tooth chemistry uncovers Southern Hemisphere role in Earth's ice age shift
phys-org.description: To understand where Earth might be headed, it's important to know where it has been. Throughout its existence, especially over the past couple of million years, Earth has experienced periodic cold and warm intervals, known as glacial and interglacial periods.

phys-org.title: UK suffers as heat breaks new June record
phys-org.description: The UK suffered its hottest-ever June day Thursday, with temperatures reaching 36.7C in the southwest, breaking a record set earlier that day as the extreme heat stretched London's ambulance services.

phys-org.title: New insight into how cells move copper out of the mitochondrial matrix could guide novel treatments
phys-org.description: Copper is essential for life. Our cells need the metal to make energy and stay healthy, but if it is in the wrong place or present in excess, copper can be deadly. Texas A&M AgriLife Research scientists have identified a key protein that helps maintain copper balance, with implications for treating heart failure and rare diseases.

phys-org.title: What people with intersex traits want you to know
phys-org.description: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, around 63,300 Australians age 16 and older—0.3% of the overall population—know they were born with variations of sex characteristics. This means their bodies don't fit medical norms about how female or male bodies should look or function.

phys-org.title: A giraffe named Gracie escaped in Texas. No one can seem to find her
phys-org.description: A giraffe named Gracie is missing in Texas, and the search for her has become a tall order.

phys-org.title: Ancient asteroid barrage may explain why early Earth had no stable continents
phys-org.description: New research led by Curtin University and QUT (Queensland University of Technology) has revealed that repeated asteroid impacts may have been the dominant force shaping early Earth, delivering vast amounts of heat into the planet's interior and delaying the formation of stable continents. The study suggests that during the Hadean—more than four billion years ago—Earth was struck far more frequently than today, with each impact injecting energy deep into the planet.

phys-org.title: Defect detection automated in diamond, other advanced semiconductors
phys-org.description: Materials scientists at Rice University have developed a new workflow methodology for measuring microscopic defects in diamond and other advanced semiconductor materials. By making it easier to spot flaws that can undermine performance, the approach could accelerate the development of more reliable electronic and quantum devices.

phys-org.title: Stem cell education platform strengthens students' identity as scientists
phys-org.description: On a YouTube livestream, Berkeley City College students carefully study the movements of stem cells to observe what they do as they become neurons: Are they moving, growing or forming new connections with other neurons?

phys-org.title: Scorching heat waves, torrential rain, all in a matter of days—it's not just bad luck
phys-org.description: After a heat wave, we crave relief, not more extreme weather. But increasingly, we have to contend with a succession of extremes—ricocheting from extreme heat to intense storms to flooding waterways.

phys-org.title: A 'direct wave' from colliding black holes reveals signature of a whirlpool in spacetime
phys-org.description: Black holes are some of the most mysterious objects in the universe, but they aren't always silent. When two black holes are close enough to each other, they spiral toward one another, eventually crashing in an enormous explosion and forming a single, larger black hole.

phys-org.title: Ultra-fast light-shaping technology could be 'game-changer' for future imaging
phys-org.description: Scientists have developed a new type of "virtual" metasurface—capable of controlling light in ways traditional lenses and optics can't—which they say is superior to the current approach, which relies on ultrathin engineered materials. The Nottingham Trent University team says the work will help fully optimize metasurface potential for a range of real-world applications and paves the way for a move from physical to virtual platforms in nanotechnology.

phys-org.title: Check politics at the door? Not at many workplaces, researcher says
phys-org.description: When people think of workplace segregation, they usually think of race or gender. Yet Americans are also sorted at work by something employers rarely measure: how they vote.

phys-org.title: We checked 2,000 museum specimens and discovered a tiny new 'ferocious' Australian mammal
phys-org.description: Australia is home to unusual mammals not found anywhere else—consider the platypus, Tasmanian devil or red kangaroo. But did you know our understanding of this continent's incredible mammalian diversity is still incomplete?

phys-org.title: Seven exotic quantum phases predicted in ultracold magnetic atoms, including topological superconductivity
phys-org.description: Strongly interacting quantum particles are key to some of the most fascinating phenomena in modern physics—from magnetism and superconductivity to topological states. Yet the complexity of such systems makes many of their properties difficult to understand even today. A research team from Innsbruck and Turin has now proposed a new theoretical framework for generating and studying these exotic states of matter in ultracold magnetic atoms in a one-dimensional lattice.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.
